items.note: A 665x565 px pasted raster, 286.5 by 243.3 pt - 68.5 per cent of the measure - at 154.4 to 440.9 pt by 313.7 to 557.0 pt, and the only exhibit on the paper that comes from a published source rather than from the team's own MATLAB session. Administrative districts are filled in five orange steps keyed 1-5, 6-20, 21-100, 101-500 and 501-4,000 under a 'Total Cases' heading in the lower-left legend, with a sixth empty swatch for 'No cases reported' and two outlined keys below it, 'Newly Infected' and 'Cases in last 21 days'. Country names print in a large maroon serif; the WHO roadmap date '04 February 2015' and its source line are burned into the image's lower right. The caption prints 5.1 pt under the art and carries the CDC page URL on its second line, which the text layer reproduces as body text - that URL is the only caption on the paper that names a source. The map is cut at the left edge of its own frame, so Guinea-Bissau is clipped mid-label. The prose never names the figure by number: it introduces it with 'countries can be seen clearly by the latest outbreak situation graph released by the World Health Organization'.

items.caption_verbatim: Figure 3. Compartmental flow of the SEIHCR (CT) model

mention.lead_sentence: Figure 3 shows a schematic presentation of the improved model SEIHCR (CT), and indicates the compartmental states and the transition rates among the states.

items.note: 294.3 by 146.0 pt of true vector line work - the paper's only diagram and one of only two exhibits not pasted as raster. Six rounded boxes in a row-major flow: S to E to I along the top left, each arrow labelled with its rate (lambda, sigma), then a dashed frame labelled 'CUM' enclosing the four compartments H, C, I and R with the recovery and death transitions drawn as cross arrows labelled alpha, (1-delta_H)gamma_H, delta_H v_H, (1-delta_I)gamma_I, delta_I v_I and psi. No axes, no numbers, no legend; the only printed text inside the art is the six compartment letters, the CUM frame title and the rate labels, all set in the paper's own equation font and therefore arriving in the text layer as private-use glyphs. Cited twice by number on p10, once in the prose above it and once in its own caption.

Printed defect: the grey envelope runs past the top of the axes and is clipped at 14,000 between days 95 and 150, so for that stretch the plot shows the ceiling of its own frame rather than the model's output, and the red curves are unidentified - the caption says 'transmission rate' and prints no value on any curve.

note:
Forty-five measured regions over twenty of thirty-six pages: 31 figure rows, 7 table rows, 7 exclusions, nothing unmeasured. The paper prints nineteen numbered figures, one unnumbered symbol grid, five numbered tables, and one uncaptioned reprint each of a map and of Table 2. Figure 1 is the only exhibit whose art comes from a published source (a CDC distribution map of 4 February 2015); the rest are the team's own MATLAB output, pasted as raster in twenty-nine of the thirty-one boxes. Only Figure 3 (the compartmental schematic) and Figure 7 (the dose chart) are true vector line work.

Two exhibits print twice, uncaptioned, and neither is acknowledged. p33 prints the delivery-location map again in the Future Work section, behind the sentence 'Their locations are presented in the following picture.', on a fresher WHO basemap - its source line reads 14 February 2015 where Figure 10's reads 4 February - with no figure number and no caption under it. p34 prints Table 2 again whole, same six coordinate pairs including the erroneous '10.5202 E' latitude, same seven-segment rules, 36 pt higher on the page, and the paragraph under it restates Table 3's percentage row as prose. Both are recorded as rows of their own with an empty caption rather than excluded as duplicates, because each is a complete second printing with air above and below it, not a fragment of the first; the counts they add to the census are the reason the note names them.

One table has no box. Table 1 on p8 - the fitted parameter estimates, 'Parameter Guinea Sierra Leone Liberia' over R0 1.51 / 2.53 / 1.59 and N 12,000,000 / 6,100,000 / 4,092,310 - carries three rules at 598.15, 617.71 and 746.98 pt spanning 414.9 pt, 99.2 per cent of the measure, and the drawing pass still returns no region for it. The cause is not width and not the grouping gap that cost paper 69 its grids: a single cell is painted with a near-white fill, 0.976 grey, at 435.3 to 483.3 pt by 726.8 to 741.0 pt, and it sits 6.0 pt above the closing rule. At tol 8 the fill and the rule fuse into one 21.6 pt cluster, which fails RULE_HEIGHT_PT at 12 pt; the two rules left over span 19.6 pt between 598.15 and 617.71 and fall under MIN_SIDE_PT at 25 pt, so the whole table disappears. At tol 2 the same page returns 90.0, 598.1, 504.9, 748.4 - the grid exactly. This is a new defect class for the lane's findings: a shade, not a rule, breaking a rule group.

The caption is the weakest part of the paper. Nine captions lose their tail to the maths layer - Figures 11 to 19 stop at the first parameter symbol, so 'Figure 13. Simulation of predicted cumulative cases in Sierra Leone from Feb 4th, 2015' is all the layer holds and the four panels' alpha values live inside the art; Figure 14's caption arrives as 'The effect of' and nothing else; Table 5's as 'Value for'. Figure 2 prints one caption under the third of its three panels, 1006 pt from the first, and it is the word 'respectively' alone that maps panel to country. Figures 4, 5 and 6 are cited nowhere but the abstract, in a single parenthetical 'The model's results (Fig.4,5,6)'. No caption on the paper states a unit, a sample, or a conclusion, and Figure 13's four panels carry no key for their four fan lines.

The mentions are thin exactly where the exhibits are thick. Thirty-one figure rows collect seven by-number citations that are not their own captions - Figs 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12 and 13 once each from the abstract, Figure 3, Figure 8, Figure 9, Figure 11, Figure 16 and Figure 18 once each from the prose, Figure 14 once from the page after it, Figure 17 once from the page after it, and Table 2 and Table 5 once each from the sentence above them. Figures 2, 15, 19, Table 3, Table 4 and both reprints record count 0. The severity analysis of section 8 is built on four figures (15 to 19) of which two are never named in the text at all.

Ruling. Every table on the paper is booktabs in the strict sense - horizontal rules only, no vertical stroke anywhere, no border - but the rules behave in three different ways. Tables 2, 4 and 5 and both reprints cut each rule into one segment per column at the gutters, which is a 7-, 5-, 5- and 7-segment rule rather than a continuous one. Table 3 draws its three rules only across the date column, 86.3 pt of a 415.4 pt grid, so five of its eight columns are ungridded. The symbol grid rules every row, 0.48 pt under each, with 1.44 pt at the top, under the header and at the foot. Widths: Table 2 and its reprint 440.2 pt, 105.2 per cent of the 418.3 pt measure, overhanging both margins - the only exhibits on the paper that leave the text block on both sides; Tables 3, 4, 5 and the symbol grid 414.9 to 415.7 pt, 99.2 to 99.4 per cent; and Figure 8's right panel overhangs the right margin alone by 21.4 pt.

Printed defects, recorded not corrected. Figure 8's caption promises 'quantity of needed medicine per week' while the right panel's axis reads 'Unit dose of the medicine needed' and the prose calls it a daily dose; Figure 7's caption says 'per day' under an axis that says only 'Unit dose'. Table 2 and its p34 reprint both print '10.5202 E' for a latitude. Table 4 prints comma decimals, 18,64% and 21,85%, where Table 3 prints 13.93% and 6.21%, and the two tables split the same 111 unit doses. Table 5's Graph 4 row opens with '0.6-0.01', a band that runs downward, and its four bands overlap one another's critical values. Figure 8's left panel is labelled 'Time (day)' and its right 'time (day)'. Figure 6 is described by Figure 18's caption as the incubation period where the axis measures cumulative individuals, and the prose that discusses Figure 15 credits Figure 14 for its black line. The heading pass is as unusable here as on papers 68 and 69: it reads the parameter block between Figures 4 and 5 as a heading ('1 Estimation of R0' lands on p12, '2 Determination of other parameters' on p14), leaves the References page as 'unnumbered-title References' and reads a wrapped bibliography line on p36 as a section of the paper, which is why p36 r1 is filed as a hanger rather than placed. Section 8's own numbering skips: the page heads read 8.1, 8.3 and nothing between.
rules: rows counts every printed row the region carries, header band included, and a grid split over a page turn is two rows with continued true on the second half only: the symbol grid prints 8 rows on p6 and 12 on p7, the taller Description cells pushing the p7 rows apart to 36.5 pt [table.rows]
the symbol grid repeats no header on its second page and still records header_rows 1, so continued is the field that carries the break, not header_rows [table.continued]

a grid whose every body row is ruled keeps the nearest closed label and states the truth in the note: the symbol grid has 0.48 pt rules under all nineteen rows, no vertical and no border, and records booktabs [table.rule_style]

a caption line in the text layer is not a citation: Figures 2, 15 and 19 print their numbers only in their own captions and the prose never names them, so each records count 0 with first_page null [mention.count]
a citation that lands in the abstract records lead_pages page minus 1: Figs 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12 and 13 are named once each on p1 and print on pp14 to 29 in that order [mention.lead_pages]
a citation that lands after the art records a negative lead_pages: Figure 14 prints on p27 and is named on p28, so it records -1 [mention.lead_pages]

a caption the layer cannot finish is quoted only as far as its last printed word, and the maths tail is described in the note: Figures 11 to 19 and Table 5 all stop at the first private-use glyph [caption.verbatim]

multi-panel exhibits of one family keep that family and are booked one row per measured box: Figures 2, 8, 13, 14, 16 and 19 hold three, two, four, four, two and two boxes, every row with panel_count 1, and none is composite-panel [geometry.panel_count]
a raster overlay on crisp vector axes does not change the family: Figure 19's red fit curves are a pasted raster over vector ticks and a vector marker series, and it stays line [geometry.family]

a filled area under named lines is still a line chart: Figure 7 inks a grey total-quantity area and three country curves, and Figure 8b inks a filled calculated area under an observed marker line [geometry.family]

a map with a pasted terrain basemap and an overlay of dots and stars is map-or-plan-view, not photo-or-raster-image and not composite-panel: Figures 1, 10 and the p33 reprint record the same family [geometry.family]
a legend printed above the axes is 'above' and one printed inside the frame is 'inside': Figure 7's four keys print above its frame and every other chart's print inside it [geometry.legend]
width is measured on the printed text span and not on the ruling: Table 3's three rules cover 86.3 pt of its 415.4 pt width, and the table still records full at 99.3 per cent [table.width]
a coordinate column of degrees with a hemisphere suffix is a numeric column: Table 2's six columns record numeric_cols 6 and text_cols 1 [table.numeric_cols]
hyphenated ranges are not decimals: Table 5's four band columns are right-aligned by column and record decimal_aligned false [table.decimal_aligned]
captions print below their figures and above their tables on this paper without exception, so every figure records position below and every table position above [caption.position]

tables.note: The first half of the paper's only unnumbered grid: a two-column Symbol / Description list introduced by the heading '3.2. Symbol Description' and nothing else - no table number, no caption, no note. Eight printed rows: the header band 'Symbol Description' at 613.8 pt and seven symbols from R0 to C(t), each description a full clause ('Number of infectious individuals outside hospital at time t'). The ruling is the paper's one register with a rule under EVERY body row: a 1.44 pt rule at 608.6 pt, another 1.44 pt at 628.1 pt under the header, then 0.48 pt rules at 647.6, 666.1, 684.6, 703.1, 721.5, 740.0 and 758.6 pt, all of them full measure, every one broken into two segments at x 196.4 pt with a 1.4 pt gap where the column gutter falls. No vertical stroke anywhere, no side or foot border, so rule_style is booktabs as the nearest of the four closed labels and this note carries the truth that every row is ruled. 415.7 pt wide, 99.4 per cent of the measure. The Symbol column is typeset maths and arrives as private-use glyphs; the Description column is plain text.

The second half of the same grid, continued over the page turn with NO header row repeated: twelve more symbols from R(t) and CUM(t) through the three transmission rates, 1/sigma, alpha, the gamma, delta, pi and omega pairs, 1/psi and kappa to the ratio of exposure probabilities. Twelve 0.48 pt rules at 72.0, 90.5, 109.0, 145.6, 164.1, 182.5, 219.0, 255.5, 292.0, 310.6, 347.1 and 383.6 pt, one above each row, and the 1.44 pt closing rule at 456.2 pt. The measured box begins at 61.6 pt on the running-head rule, which is not part of the grid: the rule at 61.6 pt spans 88.6 to 506.9 pt at 0.72 pt and is the head of the page. The last two rows are multi-line descriptions ('Ratio of probability that contact traced individual is (exposed, infectious) at time of originating case identification to the probability a random individual in the population is (exposed, infectious)') and the right-hand column of the description runs from x 201.8 pt to 505.2 pt, so the grid's 19 rows do not line up with the rule count on either page.
